context: seed: what a mature store for the reasoning-core HARD tier holds — no observation behind it; the fork is read off the family's prompt (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:106, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:115), its budgets (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:72, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:127) and the checkers (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:67, suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:82); the method is the lesson of the stream, not a convention of one instance, and it transfers from the moderate tier unchanged; regex-following at Reasoning Core level 5 (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:129): deep nesting of capturing and non-capturing `(?:…)` groups, group quantification, counted repetition `{m,n}`, escaped metacharacter classes (`\w`, `\d`, `\D`, `\W`), escaped literal metacharacters (`\+`, `\)`, `\[`, `\]`, `\.`), the `\B` non-boundary anchor, alternation, negated classes and ranges — and many patterns whose whole body is optional, so the empty string matches the pattern but the checker refuses it (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:62)
counterfactual: The overshoot is a candidate read off the pattern as prose: on `((((?:(\W))financial{3,5})))` the `{3,5}` binds only the `l` (giving `financialll`), not the word, and a `\W` read as a word character makes the whole string a non-member — the call the pass makes (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:111) then prints False before any repair. The harder-tier overshoot the level adds: a pattern whose whole body is optional, such as `(?:(([TND]MV*)?))?`, answered with the empty string — it matches the pattern but the checker refuses an empty, whitespace-bearing or non-printable string before matching (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:71, suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:72), so the witness must be made non-empty by taking one iteration of an optional or starred group.
decision: Build the regex candidate from the pattern's structure, left to right, taking each construct's cheapest witness, and only then verify it. A literal is itself; `[set]` is one member of the set; `[^set]` is one printable non-space character outside it (for a range such as `[4-l]` take a character below the range's start or past its end); `\w` is `a`, `\d` is `1`, `\D` is `a`, `\W` is one non-word printable character such as `+`, `.` is `a`; an escaped metacharacter `\+`, `\)`, `\[`, `\]`, `\.` is that literal character; `x?` and `x*` (also `*?`, `??`) contribute nothing; `x+` (also `+?`) contributes one `x`; `x{m}` and `x{m,n}` contribute exactly m copies of x; `A|B` takes the alternative with the cheapest non-empty, satisfiable witness (drop one that needs an empty string or contradicts itself, such as `\B\btwo`); a group `(…)` or `(?:…)` contributes the witness of its contents, and a quantified group repeats that whole witness; `^` and `$` contribute nothing; `\b` needs a word character (letter, digit, `_`) on the side inside the string and the string's edge or a non-word character on the other; `\B` needs the same class (both word, or both non-word) on both sides of the position; a backreference `\N` repeats group N's witness verbatim. A quantifier binds only the single atom before it: `financial{3,5}` is `financialll`, `[^yiB]{3}` is three characters outside the set; only a parenthesised group repeats as a whole (`([4-l])+` is one member of `[4-l]`, `(respond)` is the literal `respond`). The result must be non-empty, printable ASCII, with no whitespace and no backticks — the checker strips backticks and surrounding blanks before matching (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:71), so a candidate that needs them is wrong; when the whole pattern's cheapest witness would be empty — level-5 patterns are often entirely optional — take one iteration of an optional or starred group so the string is non-empty. Verify that exact string once with python3 -c "import re,sys; print(bool(re.fullmatch(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])))" '<pattern>' '<candidate>' — both arguments single-quoted — and return it unchanged.

residue: whether the chosen alternative or set member was the cheapest is judgment; the floor checks that the verified string was returned

options.name: A — construct the witness left to right, the cheapest witness of each construct, quantifiers bound to the single preceding atom, one iteration where an all-optional body would be empty
options.why: concatenating each construct's minimal witness is a fullmatch witness of the whole pattern for every construct the level-5 generator emits (no lookaround, no possessive quantifiers), and one iteration of an optional group keeps it non-empty for the checker (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:62); re and regex agree on all twelve pinned patterns

options.name: B — read the pattern as prose and type a plausible string
options.why: `financial{3,5}` read as prose gives `financialfinancial`; the quantifier binds one atom, and an all-optional pattern read as prose is answered empty, which the checker refuses (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:72)

options.name: C — enumerate strings in the shell until one matches
options.why: the budget is one call plus at most one (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:72); enumeration is refused at the third call (suite/tools.py:145)

summary.latch: a task that shows a regular expression and asks for a non-empty printable string with no whitespace that the expression fully matches, verified with re.fullmatch in the shell
not_this: a task that shows a context-free grammar rather than a regular expression — the grammar derivation rule bears there
a task that asks for a regular expression rather than for a string one accepts

summary.stakes: a candidate built by reading the pattern loosely (a quantifier applied to a whole word, a negated or escaped class filled wrongly, an all-optional pattern answered with the empty string) prints False or is refused and costs the repair call the strict pool does not have; a candidate built construct by construct, made non-empty where the body is optional, prints True first time

premises.falsifier: a pattern the checker treats `financial{3,5}` in as three-to-five `financial`s — a checker that is not a regex engine
premises.statement: a quantifier binds only the atom immediately before it, a group repeats as a whole, and neither re nor regex reads it otherwise

premises.falsifier: a pinned pattern with a lookahead or lookbehind whose witness cannot be built by concatenation, or a backreference the rule's verbatim repeat does not satisfy
premises.statement: concatenating each construct's minimal witness in order yields a fullmatch witness of the whole pattern for the constructs the level-5 generator emits — deep nesting, `(?:…)` groups, group quantification, counted repetition, escaped metacharacter and literal classes, `\B`, alternation, negated classes and ranges; the twelve pinned patterns carry no lookaround, no backreference and no possessive quantifier

premises.falsifier: a checker that admits an empty or whitespace string, or a level-5 pinned set with no all-optional pattern
premises.statement: the checker refuses an empty, whitespace-bearing or non-printable string before matching (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:62, suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:71), and many level-5 patterns match the empty string, so an all-optional pattern needs one iteration of a group to yield a non-empty witness

premises.falsifier: a pinned pattern that `re` refuses to compile or matches differently from `regex` — a fuzzy-match or recursion construct
premises.statement: the checker's `regex.fullmatch` (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:77) and the shell's `re.fullmatch` agree on every construct the pinned level-5 patterns use, escaped metacharacter classes and lazy quantifiers included
